summary: Reuse heartbeat-only roster cuts and let warm roster reads bypass unrelated cold builds

replay.detail: Disposable roster caches and read admission do not change graph replay or require recovery before the API becomes available.

schema.detail: Adds the partial covering local_observations_roster_frontier_index on (id, after_store_index) for agent harness.timeline rows. Existing stores create it automatically on their next open; there is no schema-version bump, data conversion or replay migration. Initial index creation took 0.171 seconds on an offline 1.78 GB store copy with 161,048 local observations, including 118,115 indexed agent timeline rows, using SQLite 3.53.3. A synthetic 8,701-row fixture took 0.516 ms; other store sizes and SQLite builds may differ.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or digest changes; no coordinated member upgrade is required.

compatibility.detail: Corrects the compatibility classification of the shared roster projection introduced in #1770: same-index local timeline activity refreshes last_activity_at in HTTP and WebSocket roster cards, and cached cards and pagination refs expire at current-generation work-lease deadlines even without new claims. HTTP reads observe expiry on their next request; live WebSocket subscribers observe it on the existing 30-second freshness tick. This follow-up preserves those freshness fences while making heartbeat-only local appends reusable and allowing exact warm cuts to bypass the store-wide cold-build gate. Existing subscriber changed notifications still fire for both heartbeat and timeline publications. Client response shapes and checkpoint rules are unchanged; mixed-version client/server pairs have not been separately verified.

downtime.detail: The ordinary daemon restart also creates the new partial index on first open. Index creation alone took 0.171 seconds on an offline 1.78 GB store copy using SQLite 3.53.3; end-to-end restart-to-API and restart-to-health timings were not measured. Allow time for index creation and verify API and health readiness after upgrading.

manual.detail: No new installation steps, identity changes or state conversion are required.

recovery.detail: Roster caches are disposable and rebuild after restart. The additive local-observation index does not change stored row formats; an older binary can leave it in place, and no index removal or data rollback is required for swap-back.
